entries.title: Why HN was down
entries.author: pg
entries.excerpt: Hacker News was down all last night. The problem was not due to the new server. In fact the cause was embarrassingly stupid. On a comment thread, a new user had posted some replies as siblings instead of children. I posted a comment explaining how HN worked. But then I decided to just fix it for him by doing some surgery in the repl. Unfortunately I used the wrong id for one of the comments and created a loop in the comment tree; I caused an item to be its own grandchild. Aft
entries.guide_zh: HN 解释整夜宕机的原因：手工调整评论时误建了循环引用。

entries.title: I made $200K and PayPal locked my account
entries.author: blasten
entries.current_title: I made $200K and PayPal locked my account
entries.excerpt: I'm the creator of turn.js (www.turnjs.com), a javascript library for books and magazines. I released a commercial version in July 2012 and six month later I made $200K. I don’t know how, but I made it. PayPal has closed my account because I don’t have a social security number. It seems like I don’t qualify for one because I’m just “an international student” from Venezuela. I have been working really hard to release a product for publishers that converts PDFs to HTML5 for boo
entries.guide_zh: turn.js 作者称商业版赚到二十万美元后 PayPal 锁了账户，求助处理。

entries.title: Ask HN:  How do you deal with Rabbit Hole Syndrome?
entries.author: photon_off
entries.current_title: Ask HN:  How do you deal with Rabbit Hole Syndrome?
entries.excerpt: I find myself striving for ideal and perfect solutions in parts of my work that might not matter much. Sometimes it's probably worth the time and detail, but admittedly, a lot of the time it isn't. It's just more fun and interesting to be "thorough." This happens when working on something new and unfamiliar, often side projects. In the quest for a "perfect" solution, entire branches of mathematics or programming start to beckon me, and away I go... down a rabbit hole of Wikip
entries.guide_zh: 总在不重要的细节追求完美，怎样避免工作中越钻越深的兔子洞？
